Why go: Pig Island by traditional longtail

The longtail is the local way to the southern islands. These narrow wooden boats, driven by a long-shafted engine at the stern, have carried fishermen out of Thong Krut for generations. You sit low to the water, the boat noses straight onto the sand, and the pace is slower: the crossing to Koh Madsum (Pig Island) takes 20–30 minutes, against 15 minutes or so by speedboat. With no more than 12 guests, the beach and the boat stay relaxed.

The day runs about 6 hours door to door, morning only. You reach Koh Madsum mid-morning for time with the pigs on the white sand, a swim and some shade under the trees. Then you cross to Koh Tan to snorkel the shallow reef, with the guide staying close to beginners, and have a Thai lunch at a beach restaurant on Koh Tan before heading back to Thong Krut. You are at your hotel around 14:00–14:30. The Koh Madsum island fee and lunch are both included in the 1,750 THB price.

Compared with the speedboat tour (1,450 THB, 4–5 hours), you pay 300 THB more for a smaller group, a sit-down lunch on Koh Tan and more time on each island. The honest downsides: a longtail engine is loud, there is little shade on board, and on choppy days spray comes over the side. A guaranteed dry ride isn't possible on a longtail.

Who this tour is for

  • Travellers who want a slower, more local day with a proper lunch stop.
  • Families: the small group and gentle pace work well with children. Children aged 3–11 pay the child price and infants up to 2 travel free.
  • Anyone who finds speedboats too bumpy. A longtail moves with the water rather than slamming over it.
  • Early risers: you reach the islands before the midday heat.

Who should choose another tour

  • Want the cheapest or quickest trip, or an afternoon slot: the speedboat tour.
  • Want sunset: the sunset tour with dinner.
  • Want the boat to yourselves: the private longtail for up to 8 (5,950 THB per boat), or the three-islands private boat to add Koh Rap.
  • Need shade all day: the Ang Thong big boat (from 16 December) has a shaded deck; on a longtail you are in the sun.

What to bring

  • Strong sun protection: reef-safe sunscreen, a hat that ties on, sunglasses and a long-sleeved rash vest or shirt.
  • Swimwear, a towel and a change of clothes.
  • A dry bag or phone pouch: expect some spray.
  • Water shoes or sandals for rocky shallows.
  • Cash for soft drinks, beer or snacks on the islands.
  • Fins if you want them (not provided).

Good to know

  • Sea by month: longtails stay in the sheltered water between Thong Krut and the islands. January to September is best and February to April is calmest. October to December brings frequent rain and some choppy days. Longtails are more sensitive to wind than speedboats, so the captain may switch the order of stops or, if the sea is unsafe, cancel. You then choose a full refund or a new date.
  • Shade and sun: there is little shade on a longtail, and the reflection off the water burns quickly. Koh Madsum has shade under the trees.
  • Seasickness: crossings are short (20–30 minutes) and morning water is usually calmest.
  • Pregnancy and back problems: the longtail is gentler than a speedboat, but boarding from the beach can mean wading and climbing over the side. Check with your doctor.
  • Mobility: longtails land on the beach, so you may step down into knee-deep water. Tell us in advance if you need help.
  • Children: adult and child life jackets are carried, and children wear them at all times on the boat.
  • The pigs: don't chase, lift or feed them junk food; let them come to you.
  • Drones: registered drones only (CAAT and NBTC); ask the captain and keep away from the animals and other visitors.

Pickup and meeting point

Minibus transfers to Thong Krut pier are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas cost 400 THB per person return; the booking card shows any surcharge for your area. Pickup is around 08:15, and we send your exact time by 18:00 the day before. If the minibus can't reach your road, you get a nearby meeting point with a map pin. Coming from Koh Phangan? Take the first ferry and message us on WhatsApp to arrange a pier pickup. You can also meet the boat at Thong Krut pier.
